metadata.title: Gujarat Geoenvironmental Intelligence Spatial Ledger
primary_sources: Central Ground Water Board (CGWB Ministry of Jal Shakti)
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS IS 1893:2016 Part 1)
National Bureau of Soil Survey & Land Use Planning (NBSS&LUP)
National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC / ISRO Bhuvan)
National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM)
metadata.statutory_disclaimer: Exploratory regional screening only. Not a substitute for site-specific geotechnical investigations per IS 1892 or statutory environmental impact assessments.

properties.name: Deccan Volcanic Province (Deccan Traps Basalt)
properties.lithology: Tholeiitic basalt lava flows, compact columnar basalt, amygdaloidal basalt with zeolite/quartz infill, red bole horizons, weathered basaltic murrum capping
properties.spatial_extent: Saurashtra Peninsula (Rajkot, Junagadh, Amreli, Bhavnagar, Jamnagar) and South Gujarat (Surat, Tapi, Navsari, Valsad, Dang)

engineering_significance.safe_bearing_capacity_kpa: 1200 to 3500 kPa (unweathered hard basalt); 200 to 500 kPa (weathered murrum)
engineering_significance.foundation_suitability: Excellent for heavy gravity dams, high-rise buildings, and bridge piers on unweathered flows
engineering_significance.seepage_permeability: Low primary matrix permeability (<10^-7 cm/s); high secondary fracture permeability along cooling joints and vesicle horizons requiring curtain grouting
engineering_significance.excavation_behavior: Requires controlled blasting or hydraulic rock breaker for unweathered flows; rippable in upper weathered profile
engineering_significance.slope_stability_risk: Columnar joints and red bole clay interbeds present potential planar failure planes in steep highway cuts and quarry slopes

properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India (GSI Bhukosh)
properties.source_pub: GSI Miscellaneous Publication No. 30 (Geology of Gujarat)
properties.known_limitations: Regional lithological boundary; does not reflect local joint spacing, depth to sound rock, or weathering grade variation at site scale

properties.name: Quaternary Alluvium (Gujarat Mainland Plain)
properties.lithology: Unconsolidated fluvial sand, silt, silty clay, gravel, and kankar nodules deposited by Sabarmati, Mahi, Narmada, and Tapi rivers; thickness up to 300-500 m in Cambay basin
properties.spatial_extent: Central Gujarat Mainland (Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Kheda, Anand, Vadodara, Mehsana, Patan, Bharuch)

engineering_significance.safe_bearing_capacity_kpa: 150 to 300 kPa for shallow dense sands; 75 to 120 kPa for soft silty clays
engineering_significance.foundation_suitability: Requires raft foundations or driven/bored cast-in-situ friction piles for medium to high-load structures
engineering_significance.seepage_permeability: Moderate to high in sand/gravel aquifers (10^-2 to 10^-4 cm/s); low in clayey silt layers
engineering_significance.excavation_behavior: Easy mechanical excavation; requires dewatering and sheet piling / shoring in deep excavations below water table
engineering_significance.slope_stability_risk: Deep river embankments susceptible to toe erosion, rotational slumping, and liquefaction under Zone IV seismic shaking

properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India (GSI) & CGWB
properties.known_limitations: Deep stratigraphy varies sharply between palaeochannels and floodplain backswamps; site-specific borehole logs mandatory per IS 1892

properties.name: Mesozoic Sedimentary Super-Sequence (Kutch & Saurashtra Basins)
properties.age_era: Middle Jurassic to Early Cretaceous (~170 to 120 Ma)
properties.lithology: Sandstone, siltstone, shale, carbonaceous clay, fossiliferous limestone; includes Bhuj Sandstone, Katrol Formation, Chari Formation, Patcham Formation, and Dhrangadhra Group
properties.spatial_extent: Kutch Mainland, Wagad, Pachham, Khadir, Bela islands, and Northeastern Saurashtra (Surendranagar/Dhrangadhra)

engineering_significance.safe_bearing_capacity_kpa: 400 to 1200 kPa for competent cemented sandstone; 150 to 300 kPa for weathered shale
engineering_significance.foundation_suitability: Good bearing strata for foundations on massive sandstone; shale beds require capping to prevent slaking upon water contact
engineering_significance.seepage_permeability: Bhuj Sandstone is a prolific regional multi-aquifer with high transmissivity (200-800 m2/day)
engineering_significance.excavation_behavior: Rippable with D9 dozer in shale/soft sandstone; blasting required in siliceous/ferruginous quartzitic sandstone
engineering_significance.slope_stability_risk: Alternating sandstone-shale beds along Katrol and Kutch Mainland faults susceptible to scarp failures and earthquake-triggered rockfalls

properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India (GSI Western Region)
properties.source_pub: GSI Memoirs Vol. 132 (Mesozoic Stratigraphy of Kutch)
properties.known_limitations: Shale weathering and joint orientation dictate stability; requires petrographic and point-load rock testing for bridge pier anchors

properties.name: Proterozoic & Archean Crystalline Basement (Aravalli & Champaner Supergroups)
properties.lithology: Quartzites, phyllites, mica schists, calc-silicates, dolomitic marbles, granite gneisses (Godhra Granite, Erinpura Granite)
properties.spatial_extent: Eastern and North-Eastern Gujarat Highlands (Sabarkantha, Banaskantha, Aravalli, Mahisagar, Panchmahal, Chhota Udepur, Dahod)

engineering_significance.safe_bearing_capacity_kpa: 1500 to 4500 kPa for unweathered granite gneiss and massive quartzite
engineering_significance.foundation_suitability: Superb foundation bedrock for major dams (Kadana, Panam, Guhai, Dharoi) and heavy infrastructure
engineering_significance.seepage_permeability: Negligible primary porosity; secondary fracture flow along shear zones and foliation planes
engineering_significance.excavation_behavior: Hard rock requiring drill-and-blast methods; excellent source of railway ballast and concrete aggregate
engineering_significance.slope_stability_risk: Foliation planes dipping daylighting into road cuttings pose planar and wedge failure hazards (e.g. Modasa-Shamlaji pass)

properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India (GSI)
properties.source_pub: Precambrian Geology of Gujarat and Rajasthan
properties.known_limitations: Shear zones, fault gouges, and deep weathering profiles require detailed core recovery (RQD) and seismic refraction profiling

properties.name: Tertiary Sedimentary Formations (Cambay & Kutch Coast)
properties.lithology: Nummulitic limestone, marl, gypseous clay, bentonitic shale, Babaguru sandstone, Kand formation, Gaj formation
properties.spatial_extent: South-Western Kutch coast, Western Saurashtra coast (Dwarka), and Cambay Gulf flanks (Bharuch, Surat, Bhavnagar)

engineering_significance.safe_bearing_capacity_kpa: 250 to 600 kPa for hard nummulitic limestone; 100 to 200 kPa for marl and bentonitic shale
engineering_significance.foundation_suitability: Moderate; susceptible to differential settlement if founded across limestone-shale interfaces
engineering_significance.seepage_permeability: Karstic solution cavities in limestone can cause localized high water ingress; bentonitic clay layers are impervious
engineering_significance.slope_stability_risk: Bentonitic and montmorillonitic clay seams have residual friction angles phi_r < 12 deg, susceptible to progressive sliding

properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India & ONGC
properties.known_limitations: Solution voids and high swelling clay interbeds require ground penetrating radar (GPR) and pressuremeter testing

properties.name: Miliolite Formation (Coastal Calcarenite)
properties.lithology: Bioclastic aeolian calcarenite, coastal shell-limestone, poorly to moderately cemented carbonate sand
properties.spatial_extent: Coastal belt of Saurashtra (Porbandar, Veraval, Somnath, Mangrol, Dwarka, Bhavnagar)

engineering_significance.safe_bearing_capacity_kpa: 350 to 800 kPa for well-cemented calcarenite; 150 to 250 kPa for friable facies
engineering_significance.foundation_suitability: Widely used as natural foundation pad for coastal industrial and marine structures; historic building stone (Porbandar Stone)
engineering_significance.seepage_permeability: High permeability through macro-pores and karstic dissolution cavities (10^-2 to 10^-3 cm/s)
engineering_significance.excavation_behavior: Easily cut with rotary trenchers or diamond wire saws; porous texture susceptible to sea salt crystallization weathering
engineering_significance.slope_stability_risk: Coastal sea cliffs prone to marine notch undercutting, roof collapse of sea caves, and block toppling

properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India & Physical Research Laboratory (PRL)
properties.source_pub: Quaternary Sea-Level & Coastal Studies of Saurashtra
properties.known_limitations: Carbonate dissolution voids and variable cementation require sonic borehole logging and core testing

properties.name: Rann Hypersaline Evaporite & Mudflat Complex
properties.lithology: Hypersaline marine-lacustrine silt, dark grey clay, halite salt crust, gypsum crystals, tidal mudflat sediments
properties.spatial_extent: Great Rann of Kutch and Little Rann of Kutch (>20,000 sq km)

engineering_significance.safe_bearing_capacity_kpa: 30 to 75 kPa (extremely soft and compressible saturated fine sediments)
engineering_significance.foundation_suitability: Very poor; requires substantial ground improvement (pre-loading, prefabricated vertical drains PVD, stone columns, or deep end-bearing piles)
engineering_significance.seepage_permeability: Very low vertical permeability in clay layers; horizontal brine movement under high hydrostatic gradients
engineering_significance.excavation_behavior: Trafficability failure during monsoon; high ground water table at or above surface; treacherous quick-condition in tidal silt
engineering_significance.slope_stability_risk: Severe chemical attack on cementitious materials and steel due to extreme chloride and sulfate concentrations; severe ground subsidence

properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India & Space Applications Centre (SAC)
properties.source_pub: Geomorphology of Kutch and Saurashtra Marine Complexes
properties.known_limitations: Seasonal inundation shifts soil behavior from dried cracked crust in summer to liquid soft mud in monsoon; CBR < 1%

properties.name: Kutch Mainland Fault (KMF)
properties.seismic_capability: Max Credible Earthquake Mw 7.8; Active source of 2001 Bhuj earthquake aftershocks
properties.engineering_implication: Mandatory peak ground acceleration PGA >= 0.36g; fault rupture zone exclusion buffer of minimum 300m for critical lifelines
properties.source_org: Institute of Seismological Research (ISR) Gandhinagar & GSI
properties.known_limitations: Subsurface rupture plane may diverge from surface scarp; micro-zonation required within 10 km

properties.name: Allah Bund Fault (1819 Earthquake Scarp)
properties.fault_type: East-West Reverse Fault / Ground Uplift Dam
properties.seismic_capability: Source of 1819 Great Rann Earthquake (Mw 7.8); created 90 km long, 3-6m high natural earth wall
properties.engineering_implication: Very high ground shaking and primary surface rupture hazard in northern Kutch border region
properties.source_org: Institute of Seismological Research (ISR) & Survey of India
properties.known_limitations: Remote desert location; salt crust obscures precise fault trace

properties.name: Katrol Hill Fault (KHF)
properties.seismic_capability: Paleoseismic events Mw 6.5 to 7.0; traverses 15 km south of Bhuj City
properties.engineering_implication: Near-fault directivity pulses and high vertical acceleration components (V/H > 0.8) for structures in Bhuj-Nakhatrana belt
properties.source_org: Institute of Seismological Research (ISR)
properties.known_limitations: Intermittent surface exposure; blind thrust segments south of Katrol range

properties.name: Narmada-Son Lineament Fault Zone
properties.fault_type: Deep Crustal Continental Shear & Rift Margin Fault
properties.seismic_capability: Historically active (1970 Bharuch Earthquake Mw 5.4; 1997 Jabalpur Mw 5.8)
properties.dip_direction: Steep north-to-subvertical strike-slip with normal component
properties.engineering_implication: Controls seismic hazard for Narmada dam, bridges, and industrial corridor (NH-48 Bharuch-Ankleshwar); BIS Zone IV design mandatory
properties.source_org: Geological Survey of India & GSDMA
properties.known_limitations: Deep basement fault concealed beneath thick Tertiary and Quaternary alluvium

properties.name: Cambay Rift Basin Western Margin Fault
properties.fault_type: North-South Extensional Rift Basin Normal Fault
properties.seismic_capability: Micro-earthquakes and moderate tremors; controls Cambay graben subsidence and geothermal anomalies (Tuwa/Dholera)
properties.engineering_implication: Thick unconsolidated sediments cause strong ground motion amplification; site response spectra require $S_a/g$ amplification factors per IS 1893 Type III soft soils
properties.source_org: Institute of Seismological Research (ISR) & ONGC
properties.known_limitations: Concealed beneath 2000m+ of Tertiary and Quaternary sediments; mapped primarily via 2D/3D seismic reflection

properties.name: Deep Black Cotton Soils (Vertisols / Chromic Haplusterts)
properties.spatial_extent: Saurashtra plateaus, South Gujarat (Surat, Navsari, Bharuch, Vadodara) and Bhal Tract

engineering_significance.foundation_hazard: Severe differential heave in monsoon and shrinkage cracking (cracks up to 150mm wide and 2m deep) in dry summer
engineering_significance.foundation_solution: Under-reamed bored piles anchored minimum 1.5m into non-expansive stratum (IS 2911 Part 3); or Cohesive Non-Swelling (CNS) soil cushioning layer (IS 9451)
engineering_significance.embankment_behavior: Low shear strength when wet (c=15 kPa, phi=8 deg); high propensity for slope sloughing and shallow slip surfaces; requires 3H:1V side slopes or lime-flyash stabilization
engineering_significance.canal_lining_hazard: Expansive pressure shatters rigid concrete canal linings if CNS layer is omitted (critical lesson from early Narmada and Saurashtra branch canals)

properties.source_org: National Bureau of Soil Survey & Land Use Planning (NBSS&LUP)
properties.source_pub: Soils of Gujarat: Their Kinds, Distribution, Characterization and Uses (NBSS Pub 80)
properties.known_limitations: Thickness of active zone varies from 1.2m to 3.5m across districts; field swell pressure tests mandatory before foundation design

properties.name: Alluvial Sandy Loams & Silts (Inceptisols / Typic Ustochrepts)
properties.taxonomy: Coarse-loamy to fine-silty, mixed, hyperthermic Typic Ustochrepts
properties.spatial_extent: North and Central Gujarat Plains (Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Kheda, Mehsana, Anand, Sabarkantha)

engineering_significance.foundation_hazard: Susceptible to seismic liquefaction if water table is shallow (<5m) and fines content is low with SPT N < 15 under Zone IV earthquake shaking
engineering_significance.foundation_solution: Conventional isolated or combined RC footings; raft foundations for basements; precast driven piles or bored cast-in-situ piles for heavy industrial loads
engineering_significance.embankment_behavior: Excellent subgrade and fill material; compacts readily with vibratory smooth wheeled rollers to >98% MDD
engineering_significance.seepage_control: Canal networks require geomembrane or concrete lining to prevent heavy conveyance seepage losses

properties.source_org: NBSS&LUP & Gujarat State Agriculture Department
properties.known_limitations: Stratification with loose silty sand layers requires standard penetration testing (SPT) and grain size distribution curves at 1.5m intervals

properties.name: Coastal Saline Marsh & Marine Clay Soils (Salids / Typic Halaquepts)
properties.taxonomy: Fine-silty, mixed, hyperthermic Typic Halaquepts / Aquents
properties.spatial_extent: Coastal estuaries and tidal mudflats (Gulf of Khambhat, Gulf of Kutch, Bhal tract, Dholera, Dahej, Hazira, Kandla)

engineering_significance.chemical_attack_hazard: Severe sulfate and chloride attack on concrete and steel reinforcement; requires Sulfate Resisting Portland Cement (IS 12330), low w/c ratio <= 0.40, and minimum 50-75mm concrete cover
engineering_significance.foundation_hazard: High compressibility (compression index Cc = 0.35 to 0.60); large long-term secondary consolidation settlements; very low undrained shear strength (Su = 15 to 30 kPa)
engineering_significance.ground_improvement: Mandatory surcharge pre-loading with Prefabricated Vertical Drains (PVD), stone columns, or deep cement soil mixing for port yards and roads
engineering_significance.corrosion_mitigation: Fusion bonded epoxy coated (FBEC) rebar or corrosion-resistant steel (CRS) mandatory per IS 456 Table 4 exposure Class 'Severe/Very Severe'

properties.source_org: NBSS&LUP & Central Salt & Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSMCRI)
properties.source_pub: Saline and Sodic Soils of Gujarat Research Bulletin
properties.known_limitations: Salinity profile changes sharply with tidal inundation frequency; chemical analysis of groundwater and soil extract essential

properties.name: Residual Red & Lateritic Gravelly Soils (Alfisols / Typic Haplustalfs)
properties.taxonomy: Fine to clayey-skeletal, mixed, hyperthermic Typic Haplustalfs
properties.spatial_extent: Eastern and North-Eastern hilly tracts (Dang, Valsad uplands, Chhota Udepur, Dahod, Aravalli foothills)

engineering_significance.foundation_behavior: High shear strength (phi = 26 to 34 deg, c = 25 to 50 kPa); stable foundation bed for residential, bridge abutments, and road embankments
engineering_significance.highway_subgrade: Highly suitable as road subgrade and granular sub-base (GSB) borrow material per MoRTH specifications
engineering_significance.erosion_hazard: Hill road cuts susceptible to gully erosion and surface sheetwash during high monsoon rainfall (>1500 mm in Dang); requires bio-turfing and stone pitching
engineering_significance.slope_stability: Good stability on natural slopes up to 28 deg; cut slopes at 1H:1V require catch-water drains at crest

properties.source_org: NBSS&LUP & Forest Department Gujarat
properties.known_limitations: Depth to underlying crystalline or basaltic bedrock ranges from 0.5m to 2.5m; test pits needed to evaluate hard rock contact

properties.name: Desert & Calcareous Sandy Soils (Aridisols / Typic Camborthids)
properties.taxonomy: Coarse-loamy to sandy, mixed, hyperthermic Typic Camborthids
properties.spatial_extent: Northern Banaskantha, Patan border, and Northern Kutch arid fringes

engineering_significance.construction_hazard: Zero cohesion when dry; poor trafficability of wheeled construction vehicles; wind erosion and dune migration across roads and railways
engineering_significance.foundation_solution: Requires continuous confinement; vibro-compaction or deep dynamic compaction to increase relative density Dr > 70% before placing footings
engineering_significance.water_retention: Extremely high infiltration rate prevents unlined water storage; unlined canals lose up to 40% volume through percolation
engineering_significance.highway_design: Subgrade must be confined with cohesive soil shoulders or geo-cells to prevent edge drop-off and wind deflation

properties.source_org: NBSS&LUP & Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI)
properties.known_limitations: Windblown silt lenses can exhibit sudden collapse settlement upon first saturation (hydro-collapse); plate load tests must include inundation phase

properties.name: Gujarat Coastal Lowlands & Tidal Plains
properties.geomorphology: Mudflats, barrier beaches, mangrove swamps, estuaries, saline depressions
properties.civil_implications: Requires minimum finished floor level (FFL) above high astronomical tide + storm surge + sea level rise allowance; pumped storm drainage required; tidal lock gates on culverts
properties.source_org: National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC / ISRO Bhuvan) & SRTM DEM
properties.known_limitations: Regional slope category; micro-topography, retaining wall cuts, and local borrow pits require total station / LiDAR survey

properties.name: Central Gujarat Fluvial Alluvial Plain
properties.geomorphology: Alluvial terraces, palaeochannels, floodplain levees, ravine badlands along Mahi and Sabarmati
properties.civil_implications: Ideal terrain for major highways and rail corridors; minimal cut-and-fill earthworks; cross-drainage structures required at frequent intervals for monsoon runoff
properties.source_org: National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC / ISRO Bhuvan) & SRTM DEM
properties.known_limitations: Regional slope category; micro-topography, retaining wall cuts, and local borrow pits require total station / LiDAR survey

properties.name: Saurashtra Upland Basalt Plateau & Terraces
properties.slope_classification: Undulating to Rolling (2 to 5 deg / 3.5 to 8.7%)
properties.geomorphology: Dissected basalt plateaus, stepped lava flow terraces, radial drainage network, mesa and butte landforms
properties.civil_implications: Stable foundations on shallow rock; road alignments require balanced cut-and-fill across stepped traps; natural drainage channels prevent waterlogging
properties.source_org: National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC / ISRO Bhuvan) & SRTM DEM
properties.known_limitations: Regional slope category; micro-topography, retaining wall cuts, and local borrow pits require total station / LiDAR survey

properties.name: Kutch Uplands, Scarps & Inselbergs
properties.slope_classification: Moderately Steep to Steep (5 to 15 deg / 8.7 to 26%)
properties.geomorphology: Anticlinal ridges, cuesta landforms, fault scarps (KMF, KHF), badland topography, rocky pediments
properties.civil_implications: Road cuts require structural rockfall netting and rock bolt anchors; bridge approaches across seasonal ephemeral rivers require deep scour protection
properties.source_org: National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC / ISRO Bhuvan) & SRTM DEM
properties.known_limitations: Regional slope category; micro-topography, retaining wall cuts, and local borrow pits require total station / LiDAR survey

properties.name: Eastern Highlands, Aravalli & Western Ghats Spurs
properties.elevation_range_m: 300 to 1,117 m MSL (Mt. Girnar 1,117m; Pavagadh 824m; Saputara 950m)
properties.geomorphology: Structural hills, residual volcanic plugs, metamorphic hogbacks, deep ravines, scenic ghat sections
properties.civil_implications: High cut slope instability; requires retaining walls, gabions, and soil nailing for hill roads; severe hair-pin bend geometry restrictions (IRC:52 guidelines)
properties.source_org: National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC / ISRO Bhuvan) & SRTM DEM
properties.known_limitations: Regional slope category; micro-topography, retaining wall cuts, and local borrow pits require total station / LiDAR survey

properties.name: Saurashtra Open Arabian Sea High-Energy Coast
properties.hazard_type: Severe Salinity Ingress & High Wave Energy Erosion
properties.primary_hazards: Marine saltwater intrusion up to 8-15 km inland into Miliolite limestone aquifers; coastal cliff erosion at Porbandar & Mangrol; severe cyclone surge (Cyclone Tauktae 2021 surge >4.5m)
properties.engineering_mitigation: Tidal regulators on coastal creeks; recharge bandharas (salinity barriers); heavy rock tetrapod revetments; anti-saline cutoff walls
properties.source_org: National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM) & GWSSB
properties.known_limitations: Shoreline change rate varies seasonally between southwest monsoon erosion and fair-weather accretion

properties.name: Gulf of Khambhat Estuarine Funnel & Bhal Coastal Inundation Belt
properties.hazard_type: Extreme Macro-Tidal Range & Storm Surge Amplification
properties.primary_hazards: India's highest tidal range (up to 10.5m spring tides); tidal bore phenomena; low-lying Bhal tract submerged during spring tides combined with river floods; soft corrosive marine clay mudflats
properties.engineering_mitigation: High coastal bunds with tidal flap gates; marine-grade concrete (M40+ with micro-silica) for all piling; cathodic protection for marine terminal jetties
properties.source_org: Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB) & Space Applications Centre (SAC)
properties.known_limitations: Shallow bathymetry and high sediment transport shift navigation channels and intertidal mudflat boundaries rapidly

properties.name: Gulf of Kutch Marine Ecology & Industrial Port Belt
properties.hazard_type: Cyclone Landfall, Oil Spill Vulnerability & Mudflat Subsidence
properties.primary_hazards: Very High Cyclone vulnerability (Cyclone Biparjoy 2023, 1998 Kandla Cyclone); handling >70% of India's crude oil imports creates high environmental pollution exposure to Marine National Park corals
properties.engineering_mitigation: Mandatory Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ-I) clearances; Tier-1 oil spill response equipment; deep pile jetties with automated mooring systems
properties.source_org: MoEFCC & Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB)
properties.known_limitations: Mangrove conservation buffers require minimum 50m to 100m no-development set-backs under CRZ-IA

properties.name: Nal Sarovar Bird Sanctuary (Ramsar Site #2078)
properties.ecological_importance: Largest natural wetland in the Thar Desert biogeographic province; supports >250 avian species and over 200,000 migratory waterfowl (Greater Flamingo, Dalmatian Pelican)
properties.statutory_restrictions: Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) extends 1.5 km to 5.0 km from boundary; strict ban on polluting industries, mining, and heavy commercial developments
properties.source_org: Ramsar Convention Secretariat & Forest Dept GoG
properties.known_limitations: Water level varies drastically between monsoon inundation and summer shrinkage; salinization threat from agricultural runoff

properties.name: Thol Lake Wildlife Sanctuary (Ramsar Site #2457)
properties.ecological_importance: Shallow man-made reservoir constructed in 1912; critical node on Central Asian Flyway; supports over 320 bird species, including White-rumped Vulture and Sarus Crane
properties.statutory_restrictions: Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) extends 0.3 km to 2.2 km; regulatory clearance from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) mandatory for linear infrastructure within 10 km
properties.source_org: Ramsar Convention & MoEFCC
properties.known_limitations: Urban sprawl pressure from Ahmedabad-Sanand industrial corridor requires strict monitoring of wastewater discharges

properties.name: Wadhwana Wetland (Ramsar Site #2458)
properties.ecological_importance: Century-old reservoir created by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III in 1909-10; wintering ground for >80 migratory waterbird species (Ferruginous Duck, Common Pochard)
properties.statutory_restrictions: Wetland Conservation and Management Rules 2017 apply; no untreated effluent discharge or solid waste dumping permitted
properties.source_org: Ramsar Convention & Vadodara Forest Division
properties.known_limitations: Heavily utilized for local command area irrigation; seasonal water drawdown must be balanced against ecological requirements

properties.name: Khijadiya Bird Sanctuary (Ramsar Site #2459)
properties.ecological_importance: Unique coastal wetland with freshwater lakes on one side and saltwater marine marshes on the other, separated by an earthen bund; supports >300 avian species
properties.statutory_restrictions: Eco-Sensitive Zone notification; industrial effluent discharge strictly prohibited; coastal bund structural maintenance vital to prevent seawater ingress into freshwater basin
properties.source_org: Ramsar Convention & Jamnagar Marine National Park Division
properties.known_limitations: Proximity to Jamnagar oil refineries and industrial belt requires continuous ambient air and water monitoring

properties.name: Marine National Park & Sanctuary (Gulf of Kutch)
properties.ecological_importance: India's first Marine National Park (1982); includes 42 islands, living coral reefs (52 species), sea grasses, mangroves, dugongs, green sea turtles, and dolphins
properties.statutory_restrictions: Highest statutory protection under Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972; strict prohibition on dredging, port reclamation, or effluent discharge in core zone
properties.source_org: Forest Dept GoG & MoEFCC
properties.known_limitations: Linear infrastructure crossing (pipelines, submarine cables) requires prior Supreme Court Standing Committee of NBWL clearance

properties.name: Gir National Park & Wildlife Sanctuary
properties.designation: National Park & Wildlife Sanctuary (Asiatic Lion Habitat)
properties.ecological_importance: The sole global wild habitat of the endangered Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica, >674 individuals); dry deciduous teak forest ecosystem
properties.statutory_restrictions: ESZ buffer up to 10 km from sanctuary perimeter; stringent regulation of highway speeds, night traffic bans on state roads, and underground cabling of high-voltage transmission lines
properties.source_org: Forest Dept GoG & Wildlife Institute of India (WII)
properties.known_limitations: Linear infrastructure must construct eco-ducts, underpasses, and animal crossing corridors per WII guidelines
